questions.q: What are the three core components of setting in a literary text?
questions.a: The three core components are physical setting (geography, weather, objects), temporal setting (time of day, season, historical period), and social setting (customs, occupations, relationships). A wrong answer that only lists "place and time" reveals the student misses the social/cultural dimension, which is crucial in "cukjl" where village rituals and agricultural life define the setting.

questions.q: In the poem "cukjl", the line "bl 'kgj esa olar vpkud vkrk gS" (the wave rises in this village) appears early. Explain in your own words what "olar" (wave) suggests about the atmosphere of the village at that moment.
questions.a: "Olar" suggests a sudden, swelling movement — like a wave of sound, life, or emotion rising in the village. It creates an atmosphere of vibrant, organic energy, as if the village itself is breathing. A wrong answer that interprets "olar" only as a literal water wave misses the metaphorical use: the poet is describing the village waking up or a surge of collective life, not a flood.

questions.q: Apply the concept of "social setting" to the stanza describing "fHk[kkfj;ksa osQ dVksjksa dk fupkV [kkyhiu" (the dense shade of trees on the banks of ponds). What social activity does this detail imply, and how does it shape the atmosphere?
questions.a: The dense shade implies a communal resting place where villagers gather during breaks from fieldwork. This social detail creates an atmosphere of leisurely togetherness and shared rhythm. A wrong answer that only sees "trees and ponds" as physical description fails to infer the human activity that gives the setting its social texture.

questions.q: Compare the atmosphere created in the first half of the poem (village waking, daily routines) with the atmosphere in the later stanzas ("èkhjs&èkhjs gksuk" — the gradual fading). What shift occurs, and what does it reveal about the poet's view of the village?
questions.a: The first half builds an atmosphere of lively, cyclical continuity; the later stanzas shift to a quiet, inevitable fading ("èkhjs&èkhjs" — slowly, slowly). This contrast reveals the poet's bittersweet recognition that the village's timeless rhythm is fragile. A wrong answer that says "the mood becomes sad" without linking the shift to the *structure* of the poem (cyclical vs. linear fading) misses the analytical depth required.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of the poet's use of the repeated phrase "èkhjs&èkhjs" (slowly, slowly) in creating the poem's final atmosphere. Does it enhance or weaken the portrayal of the village's decline?
questions.a: The repetition mimics the very slowness it describes, forcing the reader to experience the gradual erosion of the village. It enhances the atmosphere by making the decline feel inevitable and intimate, not abrupt. A wrong answer that calls it "just repetition for emphasis" fails to evaluate how the *form* (repetition) enacts the *content* (slow fading), a key analytical skill.

questions.q: Write a four-line stanza in Hindi that creates an atmosphere of "nostalgic stillness" for a village setting, using at least two sensory images and one time marker. Do not copy lines from "cukjl".
questions.a: Example: "साँझ ढले नीम तले धूल उड़ती नहीं, / बूढ़े बरगद की छाँह में समय ठहरा हुआ। / कुएँ की जगत पर रखी बाल्टी चुपचाप, / गाँव की साँसें गिनती रात बेसुध।" A poor answer would list images without weaving them into a cohesive mood (e.g., "गाँव में शांति है, पेड़ हैं, कुआँ है") showing inability to synthesize setting into atmosphere.
